title: Bekhorot 31
description: The close of chapter four, on ḥaverim who lapse and return, Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya the tax collector and who may inspect his own firstborns, and the opening of chapter five, on disqualified consecrated animals sold in the butchers’ market, the tithe of orphans, and why Rav Sheshet wanted his teaching cited in his name.
topics: 🔁 A ḥaver who lapses: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda, and “Return, you backsliding children”
🪑 Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya, four hundred chairs and a tax collector who repented: Rav Yosef stays home, Rabba goes
🔍 Who may rule on his own firstborns, consecrated animals, tithes and pure foods
📖 Chapter 5 opens: disqualified consecrated animals are sold and weighed in the butchers’ market, but not the firstborn and the tithe
💰 Whose benefit? Standing and valuation, and a higher price at redemption
🦂 Rav Sheshet’s answer, Rav Idi who did not cite it, and lips that move in the grave
🍋 Tithe meat folded into the price of the hide: Abaye and Rava, and the etrog sold with the lulav

a1.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְכוּלָּן שֶׁחָזְרוּ בָּהֶן אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן עוֹלָמִית, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חָזְרוּ בְּמַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן, בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא — מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן.

a2.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אִם עָשׂוּ דִּבְרֵיהֶן בְּמַטְמוֹנִיּוֹת — מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן, בְּפַרְהֶסְיָא — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן.

a3.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן קׇרְחָה אוֹמְרִים: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתָן, מִשּׁוּם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שׁוּבוּ בָּנִים שׁוֹבָבִים״. אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אִישׁ כְּפַר עַכּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּאוֹתוֹ הַזּוּג.

a4.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אוֹמְרִים: חָבֵר וְנַעֲשָׂה גַּבַּאי — דּוֹחִין אוֹתוֹ מֵחֲבֵירָתוֹ, פֵּירַשׁ — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ. חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר: פֵּירַשׁ — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכׇל אָדָם.

a5.he: רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ שַׁעְתָּא, הֲוָה עָיֵיל גַּבֵּיהּ רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף וְאַרְבַּע מְאָה זוּגֵא דְּרַבָּנַן. שְׁמַע דְּאָתוּ, קְטַיר לְהוּ אַרְבַּע מְאָה תַּכְתָּקֵי. לְסוֹף שְׁמַעוּ דְּנַעֲשָׂה גַּבַּאי, שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ: זִיל לַחֲשִׁיבוּתֵיהּ, זִיל לְקַדְמוּתֵיהּ. שְׁלַח לְהוּ: הֲדַרִי בִּי. רַב יוֹסֵף לָא אֲזַל, רַבָּה אֲזַל.

a6.he: רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: תְּנֵינָא, פֵּירַשׁ — אֵין מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ; רַבָּה אָמַר: תְּנֵינָא, חָזְרוּ לוֹמַר: פֵּירַשׁ — הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכׇל אָדָם.

a7.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַבְּכוֹרוֹת אָדָם רוֹאֶה, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל עַצְמוֹ, וְרוֹאֶה אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו, וְאֶת מַעְשְׂרוֹתָיו, וְנִשְׁאָל עַל טׇהֳרוֹתָיו.

a8.he: אָמַר מָר: כׇּל הַבְּכוֹרוֹת אָדָם רוֹאֶה חוּץ מִשֶּׁל עַצְמוֹ. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּחַד — מִי מְהֵימַן? אֶלָּא בִּתְלָתָא, וּמִי חֲשִׁידִי? וְהָתְנַן: מֵיאֲנָה אוֹ שֶׁחָלְצָה בְּפָנָיו — יִשָּׂאֶנָּה, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא בֵּית דִּין!

a9.he: לְעוֹלָם בְּחַד, וְכִדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּיָחִיד מוּמְחֶה, הָכָא נָמֵי בְּיָחִיד מוּמְחֶה.

a10.he: וְרוֹאֶה אֶת קֳדָשָׁיו, דְּאִי בָּעֵי מִיתְּשִׁיל עֲלַיְיהוּ.

a11.he: וּמַעְשְׂרוֹתָיו, דְּאִי בָּעֵי שָׁדֵי בֵּיהּ מוּמָא בְּכוּלֵּיהּ עֶדְרֵיהּ.

a12.he: וְנִשְׁאָל עַל טׇהֳרוֹתָיו, דְּהָא חֲזוּ לֵיהּ בִּימֵי טוּמְאָתוֹ.

a14.he: מַתְנִי׳ כָּל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין, הֲנָאָתָן לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ, נִמְכָּרִין בָּאִיטְלִיז, וְנִשְׁחָטִין בָּאִיטְלִיז, וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא,

a15.he: חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר, שֶׁהֲנָיָיתָן לַבְּעָלִים. פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין — הֲנָיָיתָן לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ.

b1.he: גְּמָ׳ כָּל פְּסוּלֵי הַמּוּקְדָּשִׁין הֲנָאָתָן לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ. אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹנוֹ — הֲנָאָתָן לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? הֲנָאָתָן דִּבְעָלִים הוּא!

b2.he: אֶלָּא לִפְנֵי פִּדְיוֹנוֹ. נִשְׁחָטִין? הָא בָּעֵי הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה!

b3.he: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר, קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ לֹא הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָיוּ בִּכְלַל הַעֲמָדָה וְהַעֲרָכָה, מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר?

b4.he: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם לְאַחַר פִּדְיוֹן, וּמַאי הֲנָאָתָן לַהֶקְדֵּשׁ? אַדְּמֵעִיקָּרָא.

b5.he: דְּכֵיוָן דְּשָׁרֵי לְהוּ מָר, נִמְכָּרִין בָּאִיטְלִיז וְנִשְׁחָטִין בָּאִיטְלִיז וְנִשְׁקָלִין בְּלִיטְרָא, טָפֵי וּפָרֵיק מֵעִיקָּרָא.

b6.he: חוּץ מִן הַבְּכוֹר וּמִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר שֶׁהֲנָיָיתָן לַבְּעָלִים. בִּשְׁלָמָא בְּכוֹר — בָּאִיטְלִיז הוּא דְּלָא מִיזְדַּבַּן, הָא בְּבֵיתֵיהּ מִיזְדַּבַּן, אֶלָּא מַעֲשֵׂר — בְּבֵיתֵיהּ מִי מִיזְדַּבַּן?

b7.he: וְהָתַנְיָא: בִּבְכוֹר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא תִפְדֶּה״ וְנִמְכָּר חַי, בְּמַעֲשֵׂר נֶאֱמַר ״לֹא יִגָּאֵל״ וְאֵינוֹ נִמְכָּר, לֹא חַי וְלֹא שָׁחוּט, לֹא תָּם וְלֹא בַּעַל מוּם.

b8.he: הָא מִילְּתָא אִיקַּשְׁיָא לֵיהּ לְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת בְּאוּרְתָּא, וְשַׁנְּיַיהּ בְּקַדְמוּתָא מִבָּרַיְיתָא, בְּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים עָסְקִינַן, וּמִשּׁוּם הֲשָׁבַת אֲבֵידָה נָגְעוּ בָּהּ.

b9.he: רַבִּי אִידִי סַרְסְיֵהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת הֲוָה שַׁמְעַהּ מִינֵּיהּ, אֲזַל אַמְרַהּ בֵּי מִדְרְשָׁא וְלָא אַמְרַהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ, שְׁמַע רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אִיקְּפַד, אֲמַר: מַאן דְּעָקֵיץ לִיעְקְצֵיהּ עַקְרַבָּא, וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת מַאי נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מִינַּהּ? דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״אָגוּרָה בְּאׇהׇלְךָ עוֹלָמִים״? וְכִי אִיפְשָׁר לְאָדָם לָגוּר בִּשְׁנֵי עוֹלָמִים?

b10.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר דָּוִד: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, יֹאמְרוּ דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּי בְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי: כׇּל תַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁאוֹמְרִים דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּיו בְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה — שִׂפְתוֹתָיו דּוֹבְבוֹת בַּקֶּבֶר.

b11.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר זְעֵירִי: מַאי קְרָאָה — ״וְחִכֵּךְ כְּיֵין הַטּוֹב הוֹלֵךְ לְדוֹדִי לְמֵישָׁרִים דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים״, כְּכוֹמֶר שֶׁל עֲנָבִים, מָה כּוֹמֶר שֶׁל עֲנָבִים כֵּיוָן דְּאָדָם נוֹגֵעַ בּוֹ – דּוֹבֵב, אַף תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁאָדָם אוֹמֵר דְּבַר שְׁמוּעָה מִפִּיו – דּוֹבְבוֹת שְׂפָתָיו בַּקֶּבֶר.

b12.he: מַאי בָּרַיְיתָא? דְּתַנְיָא: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים — מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ, וּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ — מַבְלִיעוֹ בְּעוֹרוֹ, בְּחֶלְבּוֹ, וּבְגִידוֹ, וּבְקַרְנָיו.

b13.he: מַאי קָאָמַר? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הָכִי קָאָמַר — מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּהַבְלָעָה.

b14.he: מִכְּלָל דְּגָדוֹל בְּהַבְלָעָה לָא? מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דְּתַנְיָא: הַלּוֹקֵחַ לוּלָב מֵחֲבֵירוֹ בִּשְׁבִיעִית — נוֹתֵן לוֹ אֶתְרוֹג בְּמַתָּנָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ רַשַּׁאי לְלוֹקְחוֹ בַּשְּׁבִיעִית.

b15.he: וְהָוֵינַן בָּהּ: לֹא רָצָה לִיתֵּן לוֹ בְּמַתָּנָה מַאי? וְאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: מַבְלִיעַ לוֹ דְּמֵי אֶתְרוֹג בַּלּוּלָב!

b16.he: הָתָם לָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא, הָכָא מוֹכְחָא מִילְּתָא.

b17.he: אָמַר רָבָא: אִם כֵּן, ״מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה״ תְּרֵי זִמְנֵי לְמָה לִי? אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי קָאָמַר, מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה שֶׁל יְתוֹמִים מוֹכְרִין אוֹתוֹ כְּדַרְכּוֹ, וּמַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה דְּגָדוֹל שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ מַבְלִיעוֹ בְּעוֹרוֹ בְּחֶלְבּוֹ בְּגִידוֹ וּבְקַרְנָיו.

b18.he: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָא אָמֵינָא לַהּ? דִּכְתִיב: ״וְהָיָה הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה קֹדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל״.

b19.he: אֵימָתַי עוֹשֶׂה תְּמוּרָה — מֵחַיִּים, אֵימָתַי אֵינוֹ נִגְאָל — מֵחַיִּים, הָא לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה — נִגְאָל, וְרַבָּנַן (ההוא) [הוּא] דִּגְזַרוּ לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה, אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי שְׁחִיטָה.

b20.he: דָּבָר הַנִּישּׁוֹם מֵחַיִּים — גְּזוּר רַבָּנַן לְאַחַר שְׁחִיטָה אַטּוּ לִפְנֵי שְׁחִיטָה,

messages.text: Continued from 30b: a run of baraitot on an am ha’aretz who takes on the obligations of a ḥaver, the last ending with Rabbi Meir’s story of the woman who tied phylacteries and then tax seals.
With regard to an am ha’aretz who accepts upon himself the stringent practices of a ḥaver, the Sages taught in a baraita:
And with regard to all of them, when they retract and return to being amei ha’aretz, they are never accepted as ḥaverim; this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

notes.he: סיפא דהך ברייתא דלעיל היא דקתני הבא לקבל דברי חבירות חוץ מדבר אחד וכן כהן שקיבל עליו דברי כהונה חוץ מדבר אחד וכן בלוי שקיבל עליו דברי לויה חוץ מדבר אחד אין מקבלין אותן שנאמר המקריב את דם השלמים וגו' בזמן שהכהנים עושין רצונו של מקום מה כתיב בהם חלקם נתתי אותם מאשי וכשאין עושין רצונו של מקום מה כתיב בהן מי גם בכם ויסגור דלתים וכולן שחזרו בהן אין מקבלין אותם עולמית כו' בתוספתא דמסכת דמאי בפ' האורז במקומו מותר בחלת אנטוכיא:
notes.en: And all of them who retracted: this is the end of the baraita above, which teaches: One who comes to accept the matters of ḥaver status except for one thing, and likewise a priest who accepted upon himself the matters of priesthood except for one thing, and likewise a Levite who accepted upon himself the matters of the Levites except for one thing, they are not accepted, as it is stated: “He among the sons of Aaron that offers the blood of the peace offerings…” [Leviticus 7:33]. When the priests do the will of the Omnipresent, what is written about them? “I have given it as their portion of My fire offerings” [Leviticus 6:10]; and when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent, what is written about them? “Who is there even among you that would shut the doors” [Malachi 1:10]. “And all of them who retracted are never accepted,” etc. [This is] in the Tosefta of tractate Demai, in the chapter [Rashi identifies by the words] “Rice in its place is permitted … in the ḥalla of Antioch.”

notes.he: פ"ה בפ"ק דע"ז (דף ז.) אגזלנים ועמי הארץ קאי שחזרו מרשען למוטב וזהו תימה למה אין מקבלין אותם דמשמע דאין תקנה לעשות עם הארץ [חבר] שמקבל עליו דברי חבירות כו' ועוד דלשון עולמית משמע שכבר קבלו פעם אחרת ועוד דאמר רבי יהודה חזרו בהן במטמוניות אין מקבלין אותן שאם חזרו למוטב במטמוניות ולא בפרהסיא אין מקבלין אותן וכי זו ירא שמים בסתר ואומר ר"ת דקאי ארישא דקתני בתוספתא דדמאי בפרק שני עם הארץ שקבל עליו דברי חבירות כו' (עובד כוכבים שקבל עליו דברי חבירות כו') גר שקיבל עליו דברי תורה כו' כהן שקבל עליו כהונה כו' לוי שקבל עבודת לויה כו' והדר קתני וכולן שחזרו בהן כלומר שחזרו לסורם וקלקלו מעשיהם אין מקבלין אותן עולמית כיון דלא יכלו לעמוד בה ר' יהודה אומר במטמוניות כלומר שחזרו לסורם במטמוניות ובגלוי נזהרין על דברי חבירות אין מקבלין אותן שגונבין דעת הבריות ואין עושין אלא לפנים אבל אם לגמרי קלקלו מעשיהם אף בפרהסיא מקבלין אותן כשישוב דכשחוזרין חזרה לגמרי:
notes.en: And all of them who retracted, etc.: Rashi explained in the first chapter of Avoda Zara (7a) that this refers to robbers and amei ha’aretz who turned from wickedness to good. This is puzzling: why should they not be accepted? That would imply there is no way to make an am ha’aretz [a ḥaver] who accepts upon himself the matters of ḥaver status. Furthermore, the word “never” implies that they had already accepted once before. Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda says, “If they retracted in private they are not accepted”: that would mean that if they returned to good in private and not in public they are not accepted; but is this not one who fears Heaven in secret? Rabbeinu Tam says that it refers to the first clause, taught in the Tosefta of Demai, in chapter two: An am ha’aretz who accepted upon himself the matters of ḥaver status, etc.; [the printed text adds in parentheses: a gentile who accepted upon himself the matters of ḥaver status, etc.;] a convert who accepted upon himself the matters of Torah, etc.; a priest who accepted upon himself the priesthood, etc.; a Levite who accepted the service of the Levites, etc. And then it teaches: “And all of them who retracted,” that is, who returned to their old ways and corrupted their deeds, are never accepted, since they could not hold to it. Rabbi Yehuda says: “In private,” that is, if they returned to their old ways in private while in public they are careful about the matters of ḥaver status, they are not accepted, because they deceive people and act only for show. But if they corrupted their deeds entirely, even in public, they are accepted when they repent, because when they return, they return completely.

notes.he: אשת חבר שניסת לעם הארץ ובתו של חבר ועבדו של חבר ועכשיו רוצין להיות שוב חבירים אין מקבלי':
notes.en: And all of them who retracted: the wife of a ḥaver who married an am ha’aretz, and the daughter of a ḥaver, and the slave of a ḥaver [as in the baraita at the end of 30b], who now wish to be ḥaverim again: they are not accepted.

messages.text: If they retracted in private, while in public they continue to act as ḥaverim, they are not accepted, but if they retract in public [befarheseya], they are accepted, as they can be trusted.

notes.he: ולא בפרהסיא אין מקבלין אותן:
notes.en: If they retracted in private: and not in public, they are not accepted.

messages.text: There are those who say another version of this discussion: If they performed their actions as ḥaverim even in private, when they initially accepted the status of ḥaverim, then they are accepted when they wish to return to that status. Conversely, if they performed their actions as ḥaverim only in public, they are not accepted.

notes.he: שלא חיללו שם שמים בפרהסיא מקבלין אותם:
notes.en: They performed their matters in private: so that they did not desecrate the name of Heaven in public; they are accepted.

notes.he: שהכרנו בהם מתחלה קודם שחזרו לסורם שהיו נוהגין דברי חבירות אף בסתר מקבלין אותם כשישובו אבל אם לא הכרנו בהם מעולם שעשו דברי חבירות כי אם בפרהסיא ובצנעה לא היו נזהרין היטב אין מקבלין אותם שגונבי דעת הבריות הם:
notes.en: There are those who say: if they performed their matters in private: that is, we recognized in them at first, before they returned to their old ways, that they practiced the matters of ḥaver status even in private; then they are accepted when they repent. But if we never recognized that they performed the matters of ḥaver status except in public, while in private they were not careful, they are not accepted, because they deceive people.

notes.dh: איכא דאמרי אם עשו דברים במטמוניות
notes.he: כלומר אם במטמוניות לא הקפידו בטהרות מקבלין דלא נתפרסם לרבים שלא שמרו טהרות הילכך מקבלין דדומה שהן בחזקתן שהיו תחילה:
notes.en: There are those who say: if they performed their matters in private. That is, if in private they were not particular about pure foods, they are accepted, since it did not become known to the public that they did not keep pure foods; therefore they are accepted, for they seem to be in their presumptive status as they were at first.

messages.text: Both in this case and in that case they are accepted, as it is stated: “Return, you backsliding children; I will heal your backslidings.”

verse.he: שׁוּבוּ בָּנִים שׁוֹבָבִים אֶרְפָּה מְשׁוּבֹתֵיכֶם הִנְנוּ אָתָנוּ לָךְ כִּי אַתָּה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ׃
verse.en:
Turn back, O rebellious children,
I will heal your afflictions!
“Here we are, we come to You,
For You, O ETERNAL One, are our God!

messages.text: The halakha is in accordance with the opinion of that pair, Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa, i.e., those who return are accepted in both cases.
messages.quote: Both in this case and in that case they are accepted

notes.he: ר"ש ור' יהושע בן קרחה:
notes.en: Like that pair: Rabbi Shimon and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa.

messages.text: Initially, the Sages would say with regard to one who is a ḥaver and became a tax collector that he is rejected from his status as a ḥaver. Even if he later resigns from his position as a tax collector, he is not accepted.

notes.he: ממונה למלך לגבות מס מישראל:
notes.en: Tax collector [gabbai]: one appointed by the king to collect taxes from Jews.

notes.he: מוכס:
notes.en: And became a gabbai: a customs collector.

messages.text: In later generations they went back to saying that if he resigns from his position as a tax collector he is like any other person and may be accepted once again as a ḥaver.

notes.he: מן הגבאות:
notes.en: Resigned: from tax collecting.

notes.he: מגבאותו:
notes.en: Resigned: from his tax collecting.

messages.text: One time the Sages needed Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya for a certain matter. Rabba and Rav Yosef and four hundred pairs of Sages ascended to his home. When he heard that they were coming, he tied for them four hundred chairs [takhtekei] to sit on.

notes.he: שהיו חכמים צריכין לו לשאול הימנו הלכות:
notes.en: Needed him for a matter: the Sages needed him, to ask him about halakhot.

notes.he: לישאל ממנו דבר הלכה לפי שהיה חכם גדול. ואיכא דאמרי חלש היה והיו צריכין לבקרו. למ"ה:
notes.en: Needed him for a matter: to ask him a matter of halakha, because he was a great scholar. And some say he was ill and they needed to visit him. (The note ends with an abbreviation whose meaning is unclear.)

notes.he: קשר ותיקן להם ארבע מאות:
notes.en: Tied for them: he tied together and prepared four hundred for them.

notes.he: כסאות:
notes.en: Takhtekei: chairs.

notes.he: עיטר להם. (עיטר להם) ד' מאות כיסאות:
notes.en: Tied for them four hundred takhtekei: he adorned four hundred chairs for them.

messages.text: Eventually the Sages heard that he had become a tax collector.
@Rav Huna bar Ḥiyya Go to your important position as a tax collector, and go to your former status, as we no longer need you.

notes.he: ילך לחשיבותיה אחר החשיבות שבחר לו להיות מוכס ואנו לא נלך אצלו:
notes.en: Go to your importance: let him go to his importance, the importance he chose for himself, to be a customs collector, and we will not go to him.

notes.he: כלומר הואיל והיה כבר גבאי ילך לו לחשבותו ולאומנותו הראשון ואנו לא נלך אצלו:
notes.en: Go to your importance, go to your former state: that is, since he has already been a tax collector, let him go to his importance and to his former occupation, and we will not go to him.

messages.text: I have repented and am no longer a tax collector.
messages.lead: He sent to them the following message:

notes.he: מגבאות:
notes.en: I have repented: of tax collecting.

messages.text: Rav Yosef did not go to him, but Rabba went to him.
We learn in a baraita that even if such an individual resigns from his position as a tax collector he is not accepted.
messages.lead: In explanation of why he did not go:
messages.quote: Even if he later resigns from his position as a tax collector, he is not accepted

messages.text: We learn in the baraita that in later generations they went back to saying that if he resigns from his position as a tax collector he is like any other person and may be accepted once again as a ḥaver.
messages.quote: they went back to saying that if he resigns from his position as a tax collector he is like any other person

messages.text: A person may inspect all firstborns for blemishes except for his own firstborns, as he has a vested interest. And despite his vested interest in these cases, one may inspect his own sanctified animals that he consecrated for the Temple, to determine whether they have blemishes and may be redeemed; and he may inspect his animal tithes to decide whether they are fit for sacrifice in the Temple; and one may ask himself with regard to his ritually pure foods, i.e., he may decide for himself whether or not they have become impure, and he is not suspected of claiming that impure food is actually pure.

notes.he: אם יש לו שלמים בביתו ונפל בהן מום יראה אם קבוע הוא ויפדם ויוציאם לחול:
notes.en: And he may inspect his consecrated animals: if he has peace offerings in his house and a blemish developed in them, he may see whether it is permanent, redeem them and make them non-sacred.

notes.he: מעשר בהמה שנפל בהם מום:
notes.en: His tithes: an animal tithe in which a blemish developed.

notes.he: הוא עצמו אם בקי בהלכות נשאל לעצמו על טהרותיו אם אירע בהן ספק ואינו צריך לילך אצל חכם אחר:
notes.en: And he may ask about his pure foods: he himself, if he is expert in the halakhot, may ask himself about his pure foods if a doubt arose about them, and he need not go to another Sage.

messages.text: The Master said: A person may inspect all firstborns except for his own firstborns. What are we dealing with here? If we say that we are dealing with a case of one person examining a blemish, is he trusted by himself to deem any firstborn animal permitted for slaughter? The mishna on 36b states that only three people may permit a firstborn animal to be slaughtered.
messages.quote: A person may inspect all firstborns

notes.he: שאין כהן רשאי לראות מום של בכורותיו ולהתירו:
notes.en: Except for his own: a priest may not inspect the blemish of his own firstborns and permit them.

notes.he: להתיר בכור ואפילו של אחרים והאנן תנן לקמן בפרק כל פסולי המוקדשין (בכורות דף לו:) בכור שניסמית עינו ונקטעה ידו הרי זה ישחט על פי שלשה בני הכנסת:
notes.en: And is one trusted: to permit a firstborn, even someone else’s? But we learned below in chapter Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin (Bekhorot 36b): A firstborn whose eye was blinded or whose foreleg was severed may be slaughtered on the word of three members of the synagogue.

messages.text: Rather, it must be dealing with one of three who jointly decide the status of the firstborn animal. And is he suspect in such a case? But didn’t we learn in a mishna:

notes.he: וכהן בעל הבכור אחד מהן:
notes.en: Rather, with three: and the priest who owns the firstborn is one of them.

notes.he: כולהו בשבילו:
notes.en: And are they suspect: all of them, on his account?

notes.he: אפי' בשל עצמן:
notes.en: Are they suspect: even regarding their own?

notes.he: ביבמות:
notes.en: But didn’t we learn: in Yevamot.

messages.text: A judge before whom a woman performed refusal when she was a minor, by declaring that she did not desire the husband chosen for her by her family, or before whom she performed ḥalitza, may marry her, because he was only one member of the court, and therefore there is no suspicion of conflict of interest.

notes.he: אשה לפני החכם מותר לישאנה ואינו נחשד לומר על מנת כן התירה:
notes.en: She performed refusal or ḥalitza: a woman, before the Sage; he may marry her, and he is not suspected of having permitted her on that condition.

notes.he: כלומר שלא היה לבדו שם אלא בית דין שלשה היו שם:
notes.en: Because he is a court: that is, he was not there alone; rather, a court of three was there.

messages.text: Actually, we are dealing with a case of a single judge, and this is as Rav Ḥisda says that Rabbi Yoḥanan says with regard to a different matter: Vows may be dissolved even by a single expert, and a three-member court is not always necessary. Here too, we are dealing with a single expert who deems the firstborn animal permitted. A single expert may rule with regard to the firstborn animals belonging to others, but not his own animals, due to his vested interest.

notes.dh: כדאמר רב חסדא אמר רבי יוחנן ביחיד מומחה
notes.he: במסכת נדרים בפרק נערה המאורסה (נדרים דף עח.):
notes.en: As Rav Ḥisda said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said, by a single expert: in tractate Nedarim, chapter Na’ara HaMeorasa (Nedarim 78a).

notes.he: רואה בכורות הכא נמי ביחיד עסיקי' דאינו רואה של עצמו משום חשד:
notes.en: As Rav Ḥisda said, by a single expert: he inspects firstborns. Here too we are dealing with a single [expert], who does not inspect his own because of suspicion.

messages.text: Why is it permitted for him to inspect them? The reason is that if he wants to avoid giving the animal to the Temple, he can issue a request from a halakhic authority to annul his oath. Consequently, he does not truly have a vested interest.
messages.quote: And despite his vested interest in these cases, one may inspect his own sanctified animals

notes.he: ואינו נחשד לומר על מום עובר שהוא קבוע דמה לו לשקר הא אם היה רוצה להוציאן לחול יכול לעשות בהיתר ולישאל לחכם ולפתוח בחרטה דהקדש טעות ולומר בטעות הקדשתיו אבל בבכור דאיהו לא אקדשיה דהא מרחם קדוש ליכא למימר הכי ונחשד:
notes.en: And he may inspect his consecrated animals: and he is not suspected of calling a temporary blemish permanent, for why would he lie? If he wanted to make them non-sacred, he could do so in a permitted way: ask a Sage and open with regret, [saying] the consecration was a mistake, “I consecrated it in error.” But with a firstborn, which he did not consecrate, since it is sacred from the womb, one cannot say this, and so he is suspect.

notes.he: ונאמן לומר מום קבוע הוא ויכול לפדותן אפי' כדשמואל:
notes.en: And he may inspect his consecrated animals: and he is trusted to say it is a permanent blemish, and he may redeem them, even according to Shmuel.

notes.he: לפני חכם ויכול לומר לא זה הקדשתי אלא אחר ולא היה מוקדש הם הכי נאמן להתירו:
notes.en: Since he could ask about them: before a Sage, and he can say, “I did not consecrate this one but another,” so that it was not consecrated; therefore he is trusted to permit it.

messages.text: The reason is that if he wants to avoid bringing the animals as offerings, he can inflict a blemish upon his entire herd before separating the tithe, which would render them all unfit for sacrifice in the Temple.
messages.quote: and he may inspect his animal tithes

notes.he: דאינו נחשד לומר על עובר שהוא קבוע דאי הוה בעי מעיקרא הוה עביד בהיתירא קודם שיעשר עדרו:
notes.en: And his tithes: for he is not suspected of calling a temporary blemish permanent, since had he wanted, he could have acted in a permitted way at the outset, before he tithed his herd.

notes.he: דעדיין אינן קדושים דליהוי כמטיל מום בקדשים ואח"כ יעשר דמעשר בהמה חל על המום דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:ל״ג) לא יבקר בין טוב לרע הילכך אינו נחשד:
notes.en: Inflict a blemish on all of them: for they are not yet sacred, so it is not like inflicting a blemish on consecrated animals; and afterward he tithes, for animal tithe takes effect on a blemished animal, as it is written: “He shall not inquire whether it is good or bad” (Leviticus 27:33). Therefore he is not suspect.

notes.he: ומעשרות להתירן במומן שלא יצרכו לאוכלן לפנים מן החומה הואיל דאי בעי שדי מומא בכוליה עדריה והוי המעשר בעל מום מעצמו:
notes.en: And tithes, to permit them by their blemish, so that they need not be eaten within the wall [of Jerusalem]: since, if he wanted, he could inflict a blemish on his whole herd, and the tithe would be blemished of itself.

messages.text: He may decide for himself whether or not they have become impure, and he is not suspected of claiming that impure food is actually pure. His vested interest in this case is not so great, as the food is fit for him to eat in his days of impurity.
messages.quote: and one may ask himself with regard to his ritually pure foods

notes.he: אינו חשוד לומר על טמא טהור דאם טמאות הן מה יפסיד הא חזא ליה בימי טומאה. ובחולין קמיירי דתרומה טמאה לא חזיא ליה אפילו בימי טומאתו:
notes.en: And he may ask about his pure foods: he is not suspected of calling impure pure, for if they are impure, what does he lose? They are fit for him in his days of impurity. And this speaks of non-sacred food, for impure teruma is not fit for him even in his days of impurity.

notes.he: תימה ותרומה טמאה דלא חזיא ליה וכי לא יהיה נאמן וכן בשאר כל איסור והיתר ובהדיא אמרינן בריש הדר (עירובין ד' סג.) האי צורבא דרבנן חזי ליה לנפשיה:
notes.en: Since they are fit for him in his days of impurity: This is puzzling: what of impure teruma, which is not fit for him? Would he then not be trusted? And likewise in all other matters of the prohibited and the permitted. And it is said explicitly at the beginning of chapter HaDar (Eruvin 63a): A young Torah scholar may examine for himself [and rely on his own ruling].

notes.he: דבני ביתו יכולין לשאל לו אם נולד ספק טומאה בטהרותיו ונאמן להתיר הואיל והא חזו ליה כשהן טמאין לאוכלן בימי טומאתו אמרינן מה לו לשקר ונאמן הוא:
notes.en: And he may ask about his pure foods: members of his household may ask him if a doubt of impurity arose in his pure foods, and he is trusted to permit them, since even when impure they are fit for him to eat in his days of impurity. We say: why would he lie? And he is trusted.

notes.he: הדרן עלך עד כמה
notes.en: We will return to you, Ad Kama [the end of chapter 4].

messages.text: הדרן עלך עד כמה ישראל חייבין · Hadran alakh Ad Kama: we will return to you, chapter 4, “Until When Must an Israelite.”
Chapter 5 · כל פסולי המוקדשין · Kol Pesulei HaMukdashin: disqualified consecrated animals, sold and weighed in the butchers’ market.
Mishna
With regard to all disqualified consecrated animals that were disqualified for sacrifice due to blemishes and were redeemed, all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple treasury.

notes.he: קדשים שנפל בהן מום:
notes.en: MISHNA: All disqualified consecrated animals: consecrated animals in which a blemish developed.

notes.he: אם מוכרין אותן ביוקר הנאת הקדש היא. ובגמרא מפרשא כולה:
notes.en: Their benefit belongs to the Temple: if they are sold at a high price, the benefit is the Temple’s. And in the Gemara it is all explained.

messages.text: In order to ensure that the Temple treasury will not suffer a loss, these animals are sold in the butchers’ market [ba’itliz] and slaughtered in the butchers’ market, where the demand is great and the price is consequently higher. And their meat is weighed and sold by the litra, in the manner that non-sacred meat is sold.

notes.he: בשוק שלוקחין הרבה ונמכר ביוקר:
notes.en: In the itliz: in the market, where many buy and it sells at a high price.

notes.he: כדרך שהקצבין מוכרין בשר חולין:
notes.en: And weighed by the litra: in the way butchers sell non-sacred meat.

notes.he: בשוק של קצבין. הואיל והנאתן להקדש. דמיהן רשאי בהן לזלזל ולמוכרן באטליז ולשוקלן. שבשוק נמכרין ביוקר ויהא ריוח להקדש. אבל בכור הואיל והנאת דמיו לבעלים אין רשאי לזלזל בהן ואע"פ שאין שוקלין כנגד ליטרא עצמה אבל יכול לשקול בשר בכור כנגד ליטרא בשר חולין. והיינו מנה כנגד מנה:
notes.en: Itliz: in the butchers’ market. Since their benefit belongs to the Temple, one may treat their [value] lightly, selling them in the market and weighing them, for in the market they sell at a high price and there will be profit for the Temple. But a firstborn, since the benefit of its value is the owner’s, one may not treat lightly. And although one does not weigh it against the litra itself, one may weigh firstborn meat against a litra of non-sacred meat; that is “a portion against a portion.”

messages.text: This is the halakha with regard to all consecrated animals except for the firstborn offering and an animal tithe offering. When these become blemished and their slaughter is permitted, they are sold and slaughtered only in the owner’s house and are not weighed; rather, they are sold by estimate. The reason is that all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the owner, i.e., the priest in the case of the firstborn and the owner in the case of the animal tithe offering.

notes.he: אם נמכרין ביוקר:
notes.en: The firstborn and the tithe: if they are sold at a high price, [the benefit is the owner’s].

notes.he: בכור הנאתו לכהן ומוכר הבשר לכל מי שירצה דבשר בכור נאכל לכל אדם והכהן נוטל דמיו ולכהן קרי בעלים של בכור ומעשר הנאת מכירתו ביוקר לבעליו ישראל היא ומשום הנאת הדיוטות לא מזלזלינן בקדשים לנהוג בהן מנהג חולין למוכרו באיטליז אלא בביתו ואף על פי שלא יקפצו עליהם בני אדם כל כך ואין נשקלין בליטרא אלא באומד ואם יפסיד לית לן בה:
notes.en: Their benefit belongs to the owner: the benefit of a firstborn is the priest’s; he sells the meat to whomever he wishes, since the meat of a firstborn may be eaten by anyone, and the priest takes its money; and it calls the priest the owner of the firstborn. And with the tithe, the benefit of selling it at a high price is its Israelite owner’s. And for the sake of ordinary people’s benefit we do not treat consecrated things lightly, conducting ourselves with them as with non-sacred animals by selling them in the market. Rather, [it is sold] in his house, even though people will not rush to buy it as much; and it is not weighed by the litra but sold by estimate; and if he loses, it does not concern us.

notes.dh: מתני' חוץ מן הבכור והמעשר שהנאתן לבעלים
notes.he: אע"פ שמפרש טעם משום דהנאתן לבעלים על כרחין מדאורייתא היא כדמוכח בפרק קמא דתמורה (דף ח.) ובסוף חלק (סנהדרין דף קיב:) גבי עיר הנדחת דדריש בהמתך מי שנאכלין בתורת בהמתך יצא בכור ומעשר שאין נאכלין בתורת בהמתך דתנן כל פסולי המוקדשין נמכרין באיטליז חוץ מן הבכור והמעשר ושמא משום קרא נפקא דאין נוהגין בזיון בדבר שאין הנאתן להקדש:
notes.en: MISHNA: Except for the firstborn and the tithe, whose benefit belongs to the owner: Although it gives the reason that their benefit belongs to the owner, it must be by Torah law, as is evident in the first chapter of Temura (8a) and at the end of Ḥelek (Sanhedrin 112b), regarding the idolatrous city, where it expounds “your animals”: those that are eaten as your animals, excluding the firstborn and the tithe, which are not eaten as your animals, as we learned: All disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the market except for the firstborn and the tithe. And perhaps it is derived from a verse that one does not treat with disrespect something whose benefit does not go to the Temple.

messages.text: It is not permitted to treat disqualified consecrated animals as one treats non-sacred animals merely to guarantee that the owner will receive the optimal price. This is in contrast to disqualified consecrated animals, where all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple treasury, and therefore the animal is sold in the market to ensure that the optimal price is received.

And although the meat of the firstborn is not weighed and sold by the litra, nevertheless, if one has non-sacred meat weighing one hundred dinars, one may weigh one portion of non-sacred meat against one portion of the meat of the firstborn, because that is unlike the manner in which non-sacred meat is weighed.

notes.he: שאם יש לו חתיכת בשר חולין שנשקלה בליטרא יכול לשקול בשר בכור כנגדה:
notes.en: And one may weigh a portion against a portion with a firstborn: if he has a piece of non-sacred meat that was weighed by the litra, he may weigh firstborn meat against it.

messages.text: Gemara

The animals may consequently be sold in the manner of non-sacred meat. When does this apply? If we say that it applies to an animal after its redemption, i.e., after the owner redeemed it from the Temple treasury, does the benefit accrued belong to the Temple? Certainly not. Once a consecrated animal is redeemed from the Temple treasury, it is in the possession of its owner, which means that the benefit accrued belongs to the owner.
messages.quote: all disqualified consecrated animals … all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple treasury

messages.text: Rather, it applies to an animal before its redemption, in which case the money accrued from its sale, which renders it non-sacred, belongs to the Temple treasury. But if so, the mishna’s statement that the animals may be slaughtered in the butchers’ market is problematic. How can the animal be evaluated after having been slaughtered? Redeeming a sanctified animal requires standing and valuation, i.e., it has to be set standing before a priest for him to appraise its monetary value and only then is it redeemed.

verse.he: וְאִם כׇּל־בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה אֲשֶׁר לֹא־יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַיהֹוָה וְהֶעֱמִיד אֶת־הַבְּהֵמָה לִפְנֵי הַכֹּהֵן׃ וְהֶעֱרִיךְ הַכֹּהֵן אֹתָהּ בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רָע כְּעֶרְכְּךָ הַכֹּהֵן כֵּן יִהְיֶה׃
verse.en: If [the vow concerns] any impure animal that may not be brought as an offering to GOD, the animal shall be presented before the priest, and the priest shall assess it. Whether high or low, whatever assessment is set by the priest shall stand;

notes.he: ודמים להקדש:
notes.en: GEMARA: Rather, before its redemption: and the money goes to the Temple.

notes.he: בתמיה. והיאך יכול למוכרו להוציא לחולין לאחר שחיטה:
notes.en: They are slaughtered: [asked] in astonishment. How can he sell it, making it non-sacred, after slaughter?

notes.he: דבהמת הקדש אינה נפדית אלא מחיים דכתיב (ויקרא כ״ז:י״א-י״ב) והעמיד את הבהמה לפני הכהן והעריך אותה הכהן וגו':
notes.en: But it requires standing and valuation: for a consecrated animal is redeemed only while alive, as it is written: “Then he shall set the animal before the priest, and the priest shall value it” (Leviticus 27:11–12).

messages.text: This works out well according to the one who says that items consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar that were then disqualified due to a blemish were not included in the requirement of standing and valuation. If so, the animal may be slaughtered and subsequently sold.

notes.he: בפ' בתרא דתמורה (דף לב:) קדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה איכא לאוקומי דנפדין ונמכרין לאחר שחיטה:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says: in the last chapter of Temura (32b), that consecrated items of the altar were not included in standing and valuation; one can then establish that they are redeemed and sold after slaughter.

notes.dh: הניחא למאן דאמר קדשי מזבח לא היו בכלל העמדה והערכה
notes.he: קתני נשחטין אפי' לפני פדיונן ולבתר הכי יכול לפדותן ולא בעו העמדה:
notes.en: This works out well according to the one who says consecrated items of the altar were not included in standing and valuation: it teaches that they are slaughtered even before their redemption, and afterward he can redeem them, and they do not require standing.

messages.text: But according to the one who says that items consecrated to be sacrificed on the altar were included in the requirement of standing and valuation, what is there to say in explanation of the mishna?

notes.dh: אלא למאן דאמר היו מאי איכא למימר
notes.he: היכי יכול לפדותן לאחר שחיטה:
notes.en: But according to the one who says they were [included], what is there to say? How can he redeem them after slaughter?

messages.text: Rather, the ruling of the mishna actually applies to a case where the animals are sold and slaughtered after their redemption by the owner. And what is the meaning of the mishna’s statement that all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the Temple treasury? This is not referring to the profit from the sale in the butchers’ market, as was previously assumed. Instead, it is referring to their initial redemption from the Temple treasury.
messages.quote: If we say that it applies to an animal after its redemption

notes.he: כשהבעלים פודין אותן מתחלה מיד ההקדש איכא הנאה להקדש אי שרית ליה לזבוני באיטליז לאחר פדיון טפי ופריק:
notes.en: To the initial [redemption]: when the owners first redeem them from the Temple, there is benefit to the Temple; if you permit him to sell it in the market after redemption, he redeems it for more.

messages.text: Since the Sage in the mishna deems it permitted for the redeemed animals to be subsequently sold in the butchers’ market and slaughtered in the butchers’ market, and weighed and sold by the litra, there is a higher probability that the owner will redeem the animal for more money initially. The owner’s later ability to sell the redeemed animal for the highest market value is in effect a benefit that eventually accrues to the Temple treasury, as he will be willing to spend more money to redeem the animal.

notes.he: דבשעת פדיונן הוי הנאה להקדש דמוסיף על פדיונן בשכר שיהא רשאי למוכרן באיטליז:
notes.en: To the initial: for at the time of their redemption there is benefit to the Temple, since he adds to their redemption [price] in return for being permitted to sell them in the market.

messages.text: § The mishna teaches that the meat of blemished, consecrated animals may be sold in the same manner as non-sacred meat, except for the firstborn animal and animal tithe offering, as all benefit accrued from their sale belongs to the owner. Accordingly, even if it is blemished, the meat may be sold only in the owner’s house.
messages.quote: except for the firstborn offering and an animal tithe offering

notes.he: שאין נותנים שום דמים להקדש על בכור ומעשר בהמה:
notes.en: Whose benefit belongs to the owner: for no money at all is given to the Temple for a firstborn or an animal tithe.

messages.text: Granted, in the case of a firstborn offering, it is in the butchers’ market that it may not be sold, whereas it may be sold in its owner’s house. But with regard to the animal tithe offering, may it be sold in its owner’s house?
But isn’t it taught in a baraita:

With regard to a firstborn animal it is stated: “You shall not redeem”, indicating that its sanctity can never be removed from it and transferred to non-sacred objects. But it can be sold after it comes into the possession of the priest, while it is alive.

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

notes.he: אך בכור שור או בכור עז לא תפדה וגו' (במדבר י״ח:י״ז) ומשמע בעלים אין פודין אותן אבל נמכר הוא לאחרים משיבא ליד כהן:
notes.en: You shall not redeem: “But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem” (Numbers 18:17). This implies that the owners do not redeem it, but it may be sold to others once it comes into the priest’s hand.

messages.text: By contrast, with regard to the animal tithe offering, it is stated: “It shall not be redeemed”, which teaches that its sanctity can never be removed from it, and it cannot be sold either, as the Gemara will explain (32a–b), not when alive and not when slaughtered, not when unblemished and not when blemished.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

notes.he: והיה הוא ותמורתו יהיה קדש לא יגאל ואין נמכר דגמרינן לא יגאל דהכא מלא יגאל כדמפרש לקמן בשמעתין:
notes.en: It shall not be redeemed: “then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed” [Leviticus 27:33]. And it is not sold, for we derive “it shall not be redeemed” here from “it shall not be redeemed” [stated of dedicated property], as is explained below in this discussion.

notes.he: במעשר נמי לא יגאל ואינו נמכר דיליף מחרמים דכתיב בהו לא ימכר ולא יגאל מה להלן מכירה עמו אף כאן מכירה עמו:
notes.en: With the tithe too, “it shall not be redeemed,” and it is not sold. This is derived from dedicated property [ḥaramim], where it is written: “it shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed” [Leviticus 27:28]: just as there, sale goes with it, so too here, sale goes with it.

messages.text: This baraita clearly states that the animal tithe offering may not be sold no matter what its status, which seems to contradict the mishna.
At night, Rav Sheshet found this matter difficult, and he resolved it in the morning from a baraita.

notes.he: ופירקה בהשכמת הבקר מברייתא. ולקמן מפרש מאי ברייתא ושני לה הכי הכא מתני' במעשר בהמה כו':
notes.en: And he resolved it in the morning from a baraita: he answered it at early dawn from a baraita. Below it explains which baraita, and he answered it thus: here, [in] the mishna, it is about an animal tithe, etc.

notes.he: בשחרית מברייתא. דלקמן. הכא במתני' דמשמע דמעשר באיטליז הוא דלא מזדבן הא בביתיה מזדבן לאחר פדיונן ולאחר שחיטה:
notes.en: And he resolved it in the morning: at dawn, from the baraita [cited] below. Here in the mishna, for it implies that a tithe is not sold in the market, but in his house it is sold, after redemption and after slaughter.

messages.text: In the mishna we are dealing with a case of an animal tithe offering belonging to young orphans that was blemished and slaughtered. Since the orphans are unable to consume the entire animal and would therefore suffer a monetary loss if the meat were to spoil, the Sages permitted its sale, and it is due to the principle of returning a lost item that they touched upon it, i.e., allowed for this.
messages.quote: and it cannot be sold either

notes.he: אפי' לרבא דשרי לגדול בהבלעה הוצרך רב ששת להעמיד בשל יתומים דמשמע ליה מתני' בלא הבלעה דומיא דפסולי המוקדשין באיטליז:
notes.en: With an animal tithe of orphans, etc.: Even according to Rava, who permits [selling] an adult’s by inclusion, Rav Sheshet needed to establish it as orphans’, because he understood the mishna to mean without inclusion, like the disqualified consecrated animals in the market.

notes.dh: במעשר בהמה של יתומים עסיקי' ומשום השב אבידה
notes.he: דמטעמ' שלא יפסידו התירו אבל לגדול לא:
notes.en: We are dealing with an animal tithe of orphans, and because of returning a lost item: so that they would not lose, they permitted it; but for an adult, no.

notes.he: שאין יכולין לאוכלו כולו ויסריח ובמעשר בעל מום קמיירי:
notes.en: Returning a lost item: for they cannot eat it all, and it will spoil; and it speaks of a blemished tithe.

notes.he: להתיר:
notes.en: They touched upon it: to permit it.

messages.text: Rav Idi, the attendant [saraseih] of Rav Sheshet, heard this explanation from Rav Sheshet. Rav Idi went and stated the matter in the study hall, but did not say it in his master’s name. Rav Sheshet heard what he had done and was annoyed.

notes.he: שמעיה:
notes.en: Sarseih: his attendant. [The printed Gemara reads “Rabbi Idi”; the Davidson English has “Rav Idi.”]

notes.he: שמעיה ואית דאמרי מתורגמניה:
notes.en: Sarseih: his attendant; and some say, his interpreter.

notes.he: הא במעשר של יתומים עסיקינן:
notes.en: He heard it from him: that we are dealing with a tithe of orphans.

notes.he: להאי פירוקא:
notes.en: He said it in the study hall: this resolution.

messages.text: The one who stung me, let him be stung by a scorpion.

notes.he: מי הוא שעקצני ונשכני שלא אמרה משמי תעקציה עקרבא שמתא:
notes.en: The one who stung: whoever stung and bit me by not saying it in my name, let the scorpion sting him: [that is,] a ban of excommunication.

notes.he: כלומר שעקצני שלא רצה לומר הלכה משמי:
notes.en: Who stung: that is, who stung me by not wishing to say the halakha in my name.

messages.text: And as for Rav Sheshet, what difference does it make to him whether or not his interpretation was cited in his name?
What is the meaning of that which is written: “I will dwell in Your tent forever [olamim]”? But is it possible for a person to live in two worlds [olamim], this world and the next, simultaneously?
messages.lead: The Gemara answers that this is as Rav Yehuda says that Rav says:
messages.quote: what difference does it make to him

verse.he: אָגוּרָה בְאׇהׇלְךָ עוֹלָמִים אֶחֱסֶה בְסֵתֶר כְּנָפֶיךָ סֶּלָה׃
verse.en:
O that I might dwell in Your tent forever,
take refuge under Your protecting wings. Selah.

messages.text: Rather, David, who recited this psalm, said to God: Master of the Universe, let people say a matter of halakha in my name in this world after I have passed on to another world.

notes.he: אלא זה [שאמרו] דובבות כלומר שאמר הלכה משמו דובבות בעולם הזה ושפתיו דובבות בעולם הבא:
notes.en: To dwell in two worlds together [is impossible]. Rather, this is [what they said], “move”: that is, when one says a halakha in his name, they move in this world, and his lips move in the World to Come.

messages.text: With regard to any Torah scholar in whose name a matter of halakha is stated in this world, his lips mouth the words in the grave, as though he were speaking.
messages.lead: As Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:

notes.he: נעות והנאה הוא לו שדומה כחי:
notes.en: Dovevot: they move; and it is a pleasure for him, for it is as though he were alive.

notes.he: דובבות מנענעות:
notes.en: Dovevot: they move.

messages.text: What is the verse from which this is derived? The verse states: “And the roof of your mouth is like the best wine that glides down smoothly for my beloved, moving gently the lips of those who are asleep”.

verse.he: וְחִכֵּךְ כְּיֵין הַטּוֹב הוֹלֵךְ לְדוֹדִי לְמֵישָׁרִים דּוֹבֵב שִׂפְתֵי יְשֵׁנִים׃
verse.en:
And your mouth like choicest wine.
“Let it flow to my beloved as new wine
Gliding over the lips of sleepers.”

messages.text: Here, words of Torah in the mouths of the Jewish people are likened to a pile [kekhomer] of grapes left to warm before they are pressed, which causes the wine to exude from them easily: Just as with regard to a pile of grapes, when a person places his finger on it and touches it, it moves and issues a sound as the wine bursts forth, so too with regard to Torah scholars, when a matter of halakha is stated in their name, their lips mouth the words in the grave.

notes.he: שאוספן בכלי אחד שבעה ימים או שמנה ימים שידחקו ויתבשלו:
notes.en: A pile [komer] of grapes: which one gathers into one vessel for seven or eight days, so that they press on one another and ripen.

notes.he: כשמתחילין לבסוס כיון שנוגע בו דובב. השמרים משמיע קול:
notes.en: Like a pile of grapes: when they begin to be trodden; as soon as one touches it, it murmurs: the lees give out a sound.

messages.text: The Gemara returns to Rav Sheshet’s explanation: What is the baraita mentioned by Rav Sheshet, upon which he based his resolution? As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.quote: an animal tithe offering belonging to young orphans

notes.he: דאמרן לעיל ושנייה מברייתא:
notes.en: What is the baraita: that we mentioned above, “and he resolved it from a baraita.”

notes.he: דאמרן ופרקה מברייתא:
notes.en: What is the baraita: that we mentioned, “and he resolved it from a baraita.”

messages.text: With regard to an animal tithe offering of young orphans, one may sell it. And with regard to an animal tithe offering that one has slaughtered, whose meat may not be sold, one may include the cost of the meat in the cost of its negligent parts, thereby inflating the cost of those parts, i.e., the animal’s hide, its fat, its sinews, and its horns, which are permitted to be sold.

notes.he: דאסור למכור בשר אלא החלב והעור והגידין ימכור ויבליע לו בהן דמי הבשר שימכור לו העור והגידין ביוקר כמה ששוה הכל ויתן לו הבשר במתנה:
notes.en: He includes it in its fat: for it is forbidden to sell the meat, only the fat, the hide and the sinews; he sells and includes in them the price of the meat, selling him the hide and the sinews dearly, for as much as the whole is worth, and gives him the meat as a gift.

notes.he: דאסור למכור הבשר אלא החלב והעור והגידין ויש לדקדק מכאן דאפי' מאן דאסר לקמן (בכורות דף לב:) להמנות עובד כוכבים על הבכור חלבו מיהא שרי דכעור חשיב ליה כיון דאסור באכילה לישראל ומיהו שמנו של גיד דלא אסור מדאורייתא איפשר דאסור אבל הלכה כרבי עקיבא דשרי לעובד כוכבים אפי' הבשר כמו שמפרש לקמן:
notes.en: He includes it in its fat: for it is forbidden to sell the meat, but [one may sell] the fat, the hide and the sinews. One can infer from here that even according to the one who forbids below (Bekhorot 32b) registering a gentile [as a partner] in a firstborn, its fat at least is permitted, since it is regarded like the hide, because it is forbidden to a Jew to eat. However, the fat of the sinew, which is not forbidden by Torah law, may be forbidden. But the halakha follows Rabbi Akiva, who permits [this] to a gentile even for the meat, as is explained below.

notes.he: שמוכר לו העור כ"כ ביוקר כדי שיהו דמי בשר מובלעין לתוכו וכן בחלבו וגידו ובקרניו דמותרין למכור דלאו בני אכילה נינהו. מכלל דמעשר של גדול:
notes.en: He includes it in its hide: he sells him the hide so dearly that the value of the meat is included in it, and likewise in its fat, its sinew and its horns, which may be sold, since they are not food. By inference, the tithe of an adult [may not be sold even by inclusion].

messages.text: What is the tanna of the baraita saying? Initially, the baraita stated that one may sell the meat of an animal tithe offering belonging to young orphans, which indicates that this may be done in the normal fashion. The baraita then proceeds to state that the sale of the meat must be performed in the indirect manner of inclusion.
messages.quote: one may sell it … one may include the cost of the meat

notes.he: מעיקרא תני מוכרין אותו דמשמע כדרכו והדר תני מבליעו:
notes.en: What is it saying: first it teaches “one may sell it,” which implies in its usual way, and then it teaches “he includes it.”

messages.text: The baraita is actually referring to only one case, and this is what it is saying: With regard to the meat of an animal tithe offering of young orphans, it may be sold, but only by means of inclusion.

One can conclude by inference from this baraita that in the case of an animal tithe offering of an adult, i.e., a non-orphan, its meat may not be sold even by means of inclusion. What is different in this case from that which is taught in a mishna:

notes.he: שאינו יתום:
notes.en: Of an adult: one who is not an orphan.

messages.text: In the case of one who purchases a lulav from another, who is an am ha’aretz, during the Sabbatical Year, the seller gives him an etrog together with the lulav as a gift, as it is not permitted for one to purchase the etrog during the Sabbatical Year, and one may not give the value of Sabbatical-Year produce to an am ha’aretz, lest he engage in commerce with it, which is prohibited.

notes.he: לוקח אדם בשביעית מעם הארץ פירות שנלקטו בשביעית משום דבת ששית שנכנסת לשביעית היא וכל האילנות הולכין אחר חנטה חוץ מאתרוג ואתרוג אינו רשאי ליקח בשביעית אע"ג דחנטה בששית משום דאתרוג בתר לקיטה אזלינן ופירות שביעית היא ואין מוסרין דמי פירות שביעית לעם הארץ שעושה בהם סחורה ואינו מבערן בזמן הביעור כשכלה לחיה שבשדה:
notes.en: One who buys a lulav: a person may buy in the Sabbatical Year, from an am ha’aretz, produce picked in the Sabbatical Year, because [the lulav] is of the sixth year that entered the Sabbatical Year, and all trees follow the budding, except for the etrog. And he may not buy an etrog in the Sabbatical Year, even though it budded in the sixth, because for an etrog we follow the picking, and it is Sabbatical-Year produce; and one does not hand the money of Sabbatical-Year produce to an am ha’aretz, who trades with it and does not remove it at the time of removal, when it has ceased [from the field] for the wild animals.

notes.he: מותר למכור. לפי שאינו פירי:
notes.en: A lulav in the Sabbatical Year: may be sold, because it is not fruit.

notes.he: שאינו רשאי למכור פירי:
notes.en: An etrog as a gift: for he may not sell fruit.

messages.text: And we discussed this mishna and asked: If the seller did not want to give him the etrog as a gift, what is the halakha? How can the buyer receive the etrog?
messages.quote: the seller gives him an etrog together with the lulav as a gift

messages.text: The seller includes the value of the etrog in the cost of the lulav. The buyer should purchase the lulav at an elevated price to cover the cost of the etrog as well.
messages.quote: did not want to give him the etrog as a gift

messages.text: If inclusion is allowed in the case of the etrog, why would it not be permitted in the case of the meat of an animal tithe offering belonging to an adult?

There, in the case of the etrog, the matter is not evident, whereas here, with regard to the meat of an animal tithe offering, the matter is evident. The inclusion of the cost of the etrog in the elevated cost of the lulav is not evident, as it is reasonable that the price of a lulav might fluctuate. By contrast, inflating the cost of the negligible parts of the animal tithe offering to include the cost of its expensive meat is obviously an artifice and is therefore not permitted.

notes.he: משום דדמיו קלים ואינו ניכר שהבליעם בלולב אבל הכא אפילו דבהבלעה נמי מוכחא מילתא דמוכר הבשר דהדבר ידוע שאין עור נמכר כולי האי בדמים יקרים:
notes.en: There the matter is not evident: because its price is low, and it is not noticeable that he included them in the lulav. But here, even by inclusion it is evident that he is selling the meat, for it is known that a hide does not sell for such a high price.

notes.he: התם בהבלעה באתרוג לא מוכחא מילתא דמוכר לו אתרוג משום דדמי אתרוג אינו אלא פשוט ואינו מגוף הלולב ולא מינכרא מילתא דהבלעה כלל אבל הכא כי זבין ליה עור בהמה בדמי בשר ובדמי עור מוכחא מילתא דזבין ליה בשר בהבלעה להכי דגדול אפי' בהבלעה לא:
notes.en: There, with inclusion of the etrog, the matter is not evident that he is selling him an etrog, because the price of an etrog is only small, and it is not part of the lulav itself, so the inclusion is not noticeable at all. But here, when he sells him an animal’s hide for the price of meat and the price of hide, it is evident that he is selling him meat by inclusion. Therefore for an adult, even by inclusion, no.

messages.text: If so, that the baraita is referring to only one case, why do I need it to use the expression: Animal tithe offering, twice?
messages.quote: this is what it is saying: With regard to the meat of an animal tithe offering of young orphans, it may be sold, but only by means of inclusion

notes.he: דכולה חדא קתני:
notes.en: If so: that it all teaches a single case.

notes.he: מעשר בהמה דתני בברייתא ל"ל:
notes.en: Twice: why do I need “animal tithe” that the baraita teaches [twice]?

notes.dh: אם כן מעשר בהמה מעשר בהמה תרי זימני ל"ל
notes.he: יש מקומות דדייק כי האי גוונא בריש בבא מציעא (דף ב.) גבי זה אומר אני מצאתיה דפריך והא זה וזה קתני ובריש נדרים (דף ד:) פריך אסור אסור למה לי ובריש סנהדרין (דף ג.) פריך שלשה שלשה למה לי עוד בההוא פירקא (דף ח.) וכי תימא פרושי קא מפרש מאי זמון ברכת זמון והתניא זמון שלשה וברכת הזמון בשלשה ובפ' בתרא דמועד קטן (דף כב:) דמפרש לשמחה ולמריעות שלשים יום פריך והתניא לשמחה שלשים ולמריעות שלשים יום ובפרק בית כור (ב"ב דף קד.) פריך אני מוכר לך אני מוכר לך תרי זימני למה לי ותימה דבכמה דוכתי לא פריך כי האי גוונא בפ"ק דחולין (דף טז:) גבי נעץ סכין בכותל ושחט בה שחיטתו כשירה דקאמר התם פרושי קא מפרש מאי במחובר לקרקע סכין דלא מבטל ליה ולא פריך שחיטתו כשירה תרי זימני למה לי ובפרק גיד הנשה (חולין דף צח.) גבי ביצים טהורות ששלקן עם ביצים טמאות דקאמר פרושי קא מפרש ולא פריך אסורות אסורות למה לי ובפ' כל הבשר (חולין דף קיג.) גדג טהור שמלחו עם דג טמא דקאמר פרושי קא מפרש ולא פריך מותר מותר למה לי ובהגוזל קמא (ב"ק דף צח:) גבי נתן לאומנין וקלקלו דקאמר פרושי קמפרש ולא קאמר חייבין לשלם תרי זימני למה לי ובגיטין פ' השולח (גיטין ד' מב:) גבי כל נכסי נתונים לפלוני ופלוני עבדי דקאמר פרושי קמפרש ולא פריך ולא קנו ולא קנו למה לי וי"ל דבכל הני דוכתי דפריך תרי זימני למה לי לא שייך לומר כל כך פרושי קמפרש כמו בהנך דוכתי דלא פריך:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot list places where the Gemara objects in the same way to a repeated word: Bava Metzia 2a (“this one says, I found it”: “but it teaches ‘this and this’”), Nedarim 4b (“forbidden, forbidden, why do I need it?”), Sanhedrin 3a (“three, three, why do I need it?”), Sanhedrin 8a (on zimmun and the blessing of zimmun with three), Mo’ed Katan 22b (“for joy and for distress, thirty days”) and Bava Batra 104a (“I sell you, I sell you, why twice?”). They ask why in several other places the Gemara says the text “is merely explaining” and does not object to the repetition: Ḥullin 16b (a knife stuck in a wall: “its slaughter is valid”), Ḥullin 98a (pure eggs boiled with impure ones: “forbidden”), Ḥullin 113a (a pure fish salted with an impure one: “permitted”), Bava Kamma 98b (one gave to craftsmen and they damaged it: “liable to pay”) and Gittin 42b (“all my property is given to so-and-so” and “so-and-so my slave”: “they have not acquired”). They answer that in the places where the Gemara objects “why twice?”, it is not as plausible to say “it is merely explaining” as it is in the places where it does not object. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: כדתריץ אביי דמעשר בהמה של יתומים ביוצא המוכר אותו מבליעו כו' מעשר בהמה מעשר בהמה דקאמר ברייתא תרי זמני למה לי אלא אמר רבא כו':
notes.en: Rava said: If so, as Abaye answered, that an animal tithe of orphans [a printed note suggests reading: is dealt with in the manner of the latter clause, “one who sells it includes it”], why does the baraita say “animal tithe,” “animal tithe,” twice? Rather, Rava said, etc.

messages.text: The baraita is discussing two distinct cases, and this is what the tanna is saying: With regard to the meat of an animal tithe offering of young orphans, one may sell it in its usual manner, but in the case of an animal tithe offering belonging to an adult that was slaughtered, one may sell its meat only by means of including its cost in the elevated price of the animal’s hide, its fat, its sinews, and its horns.

From where do I say that the meat of an animal tithe offering belonging to an adult may be sold by inclusion? As it is written with regard to the animal tithe offering: “Then both it and that for which it is substituted shall be holy; it shall not be redeemed”. This indicates that a non-sacred animal designated as a substitute for an animal tithe offering assumes sacred status, while the animal tithe offering retains its sacred status as well.

verse.he: לֹא יְבַקֵּר בֵּין־טוֹב לָרַע וְלֹא יְמִירֶנּוּ וְאִם־הָמֵר יְמִירֶנּוּ וְהָיָה־הוּא וּתְמוּרָתוֹ יִהְיֶה־קֹּדֶשׁ לֹא יִגָּאֵל׃
verse.en: One must not look out for good as against bad, or make substitution for it. If one does make substitution for it, then it and its substitute shall both be holy: it cannot be redeemed.

messages.text: As stated earlier, the phrase “it shall not be redeemed” is interpreted as referring to the prohibition against selling the animal tithe offering. The verse’s juxtaposition of substitution and the prohibition against selling an animal tithe offering indicates a similarity between the two.

notes.he: במעשר בהמה כתיב ומהאי לא יגאל נפקא לן דאינו נמכר הילכך כי אסריה קרא למכור דומיא דעשיית תמורה הוא דאסר ליה:
notes.en: Then both it and its substitute: this is written of animal tithe, and from this “it shall not be redeemed” we derive that it is not sold. Therefore, when the verse forbids selling it, it forbids it in the same way as making a substitute.

messages.text: When does an animal tithe offering render consecrated as a substitute a non-sacred animal for which it is exchanged? Only when the animal tithe offering is alive, as substitution is invalid after its death. Similarly, when may the animal tithe offering not be redeemed, i.e., sold? When it is alive. It may be inferred from here that it may be redeemed, i.e., sold, after its slaughter.

notes.he: ה"נ אימתי אינו נגאל לא אמרה תורה אלא מחיים אבל לאחר שחיטה נמכר:
notes.en: When does it make a substitute? While alive: so too, when is it not redeemed? The Torah said this only while it is alive; but after slaughter it may be sold.

notes.he: אינו נמכר:
notes.en: When is it not redeemed: [that is,] not sold.

messages.text: This teaches that by Torah law, the meat of an animal tithe offering may be sold once the animal has been slaughtered. The Sages decreed that an animal tithe offering may not be sold after its slaughter, due to the concern that one might sell it before its slaughter.

It was only with regard to an item that is appraised when the animal is alive, i.e., its meat, which gives the animal its primary value, that the Sages decreed that it may not be sold even after its slaughter, due to the concern that one might sell the animal before its slaughter.

notes.dh: ורבנן גזרו לאחר שחיטה אטו לפני שחיטה
notes.he: כדקתני לעיל אינו נמכר לא חי ולא שחוט:
notes.en: And the Sages decreed after slaughter on account of before slaughter: as was taught above: it is not sold, neither alive nor slaughtered.

notes.he: נמכר מחיים כגון הבשר שכל חשיבות דבהמה אינו אלא בבשר גזור רבנן לאחר שחיטה:
notes.en: An item that is appraised: sold while alive, such as the meat, for the whole worth of an animal lies only in the meat; [for this] the Sages decreed after slaughter.

notes.he: היינו בשר דאדם שם מחיים כמה שוה הבכור גזרו רבנן לאחר שחיטה דאינו נמכר אטו קודם שחיטה דאסור:
notes.en: An item that is appraised while alive: that is the meat, for a person appraises while it is alive how much the firstborn [so the text; the discussion is of the tithe] is worth. The Sages decreed that after slaughter it is not sold, on account of before slaughter, when it is forbidden.

messages.caption: Selling the meat of an animal tithe: how Abaye and Rava read the baraita.

messages.text: Continued on 32a: Rava turns to the parts that are not appraised while the animal is alive, such as the hide and the sinews, and to the orphans, for whom the Sages kept the Torah law.
